summary: Targi is a tight two-player worker placement and card-drafting game where players place their two figures on a shared 5x5 grid to gather resources and tribe cards, aiming to build the most valuable set of tribe abilities. It's a dense, puzzly duel with very little downtime and constant tension over which grid spots to claim first.
praised: Rich combos from tribe card synergies
Quick turns keep both players engaged
High replayability for a small box
criticised: Can feel a bit mathy or dry for some
Early tribe card draws can feel imbalanced
Rules for the grid take a game or two to internalize

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking on a shared grid
interaction.detail: Both players place figures on the same central grid, and taking a space denies it to the opponent for that round, creating constant tactical blocking. The central board is fully shared while each player's tribe card tableau and resources remain private.

subsystems: worker-placement resource gathering to acquire tribe cards
sources: big tribe card bonuses (built from 5-card sets)
scoring.how_you_win: Place your two meeples each round on the board's border and center to gather goods and gold, spending them on small and big tribe cards; when the big tribe card deck runs out the game ends, and whoever's cards and leftovers total the most points wins.
